owner_posts.post_text:
Your heart doesn’t always show warning signs until it’s too late. 🫀
Regular heart screening helps detect problems early - before they become serious. Conditions like high blood pressure, blocked arteries, and heart disease can develop silently.
 ✔ Early detection
 ✔ Better prevention
 ✔ Timely treatment
Don’t wait for symptoms. Make heart screening a priority.

You’ve seen these in prescriptions and reports… but do you actually know what they mean? 

Medical short forms are used every day — but understanding them can help you stay more informed about your own health.

From diagnosis to treatment, every term has a meaning that matters.
Stay aware. Stay informed.

Before any cardiac or structural heart procedure, there is a crucial step most people never see — the discussion.
An interventional cardiologist and a cardiac anesthetist carefully review:
• CT and Echo imaging
• Valve anatomy and measurements
• Access route planning
• Hemodynamic considerations
• Patient-specific risks
• Emergency preparedness
In procedures like TAVI, complex angioplasty, valve repair, or vascular interventions — outcomes depend not just on skill in the cath lab, but on clarity before entering it.

Inside the Cath Lab during a TAVI (Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) procedure - a minimally invasive treatment for severe aortic valve disease.
Through a small access in the groin, a new valve is carefully guided to the heart and deployed to restore normal blood flow, avoiding the need for open-heart surgery.
At HVS Hospitals, advanced imaging, experienced structural heart specialists, and coordinated team care make complex procedures safer and more effective for patients.

Heart Disease in Young Adults: Is It Increasing in Metro Cities?

It’s becoming common. In 2026, ICUs aren’t just full of elders – young patients are frequently admitted too. Doctors now see this so often they hardly blink. What used to be rare before age sixty shows up decades earlier.

A shift few saw coming! Life’s pace here plays its part. Stress piles on without warning signs. Bodies react in ways we’re only beginning to grasp. Food choices matter more than some think. Movement – or the lack of it – shapes outcomes quietly (& certainly). These changes didn’t arrive overnight. Yet here they are, reshaping health across the city of Mumbai. And it’s not only Mumbai, but cardiac problems with young people are being observed everywhere.

After a heart attack or angioplasty, one question often goes unasked but matters deeply.
When is it safe to resume physical intimacy?
Dr. Kunal Patankar breaks the silence and shares clear, medical guidance to help patients regain confidence and peace of mind after cardiac recovery.

Modern cancer treatment is no longer limited to oncology alone — it thrives on collaboration across multiple specialties.

At HVS Hospitals, our Vascular & Interventional Radiology team plays a vital role in comprehensive cancer care, offering targeted tumour therapies, safe vascular access for chemotherapy, management of cancer-related clots, and cardiovascular protection during treatment.

Globally, Interventional Radiology is increasingly recognised as the fourth pillar of cancer care, alongside oncology, surgery, and radiation — enabling precise, minimally invasive treatments with improved patient outcomes.

This World Cancer Day, we reaffirm our commitment to supporting cancer patients with advanced technology, multidisciplinary expertise, and compassionate care.

PAD – A Silent Threat to Your Legs and Heart 🦵🫀
 Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD) reduces blood flow to your limbs, especially your legs. Many dismiss it as “just aging,” but it’s often the sign of something deeper — like clogged arteries.
⚠️ Watch out for:
 • Pain while walking
 • Cold feet or numbness
 • Wounds that don’t heal
 • Shiny, smooth skin on legs
🎯 At Risk?
 You may be, if you’re diabetic, a smoker, over 50, or have high cholesterol.
✅ At HVS Hospitals, we offer:
 • Doppler screening
 • Expert vascular consultation
 • Angioplasty & stenting for PAD
Don’t wait for symptoms to get worse.
 Walk in for a quick check — your legs will thank you.

Advanced heart treatment no longer requires big cuts or long hospital stays.

Heart Bypass Surgery Can Make a Difference
Blocked arteries can reduce blood flow to the heart. Bypass surgery creates a new pathway, restoring healthy circulation.
Improves heart function, Relieves chest pain, Enhances quality of life.

Diabetes is a disease in which the blood vessels are the first and most severely affected.
Whenever blood vessels are affected, atherosclerosis develops. Due to damage, platelet plugs start forming, and cholesterol begins to accumulate in these areas. As a result, the arteries gradually start getting blocked.
Because of this, heart attacks become very common in diabetic patients.
Happy Republic Day

Common Heart Tests & What They Detect
ECG (Electrocardiogram) - Records the heart’s electrical activity to detect rhythm problems & signs of a past or ongoing heart attack.
Stress Test (TMT) - Checks how well the heart works during exercise or stress and helps identify hidden blockages.
2D Echo (Echocardiography) - An ultrasound test that shows heart size, pumping strength, and valve function.
Invasive Coronary Angiography - Gold standard test to find heart artery blockages and decide the best treatment.
Each Heart Test Has A Specific Purpose - Doctors choose the right test based on symptoms, risk factors, and clinical assessment.

featured_reviews.name: Anuj Saini
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear All,
Iam a Civil Engineer professional and working with one of the top most construction company in India.
As per company policy, I was asked to undergo a medical checkup referred by the company. These medical checkups are in the panel of the company and I got my tests done from one of the reputed Health experts in Navi Mumbai.

Unfortunately the result turned out to be shocking and a heart blockage was detected.  Being a sports athlete, I couldn't digest the scenario and was shocked & totally devastated.

I was asked to redo the medical test on my own expenditure and confirm to my client if Iam fit for the company.

I happened to call many cardiologists and was lucky enough to get in touch with Dr. BRIJESH AGRAWAL - Cardiologist, Interventional Cardiologist.
Thanks to Ms. Sonal from the receptionist who helped me with  booking the appointment on the spot and solved all my queries. I asked her many questions with respect to the tests done, experience of the doctor, fees etc. I found her professional, smart and quick which made me very comfortable.
Dr. Brijesh Agrawal heart clinic is in Chembur above Malhar Hotel. It was crowded with patients but we were taken inside at the right time slot. inshort, we didn't have to wait for hours like I did in my previous health checkup experience.
Dr. Agrawal is a very knowledgeable and down to earth person.  He is 40+ years old and an interventional cardiologist with more than 15 to 20 years of experience in cardiology, but looks like a teenager :)

He saw all my old reports (2 days old report which shows blockage) and asked me to do a 2D EchoCardiography and Tread mill test.
With the blessings of God, Iam perfectly alright and the previous report turned out to be wrong.
Dr. Brijesh Agrawal explained in detail about Heart functions, how 2D  EchoCardiography would be carried out and I was in total ease before entering the 2D room.
The room was very neat and clean and the equipment looked to be of latest make. I was asked to lay on one side and then a colourless gel was applied to the chest area. Then Dr. Agrawal moved the transducer across the various parts of his chest to get specific/desired views of the heart.
I was happy to see that he was doing it personally and was not dependent on any technician to do it for him.

After 2D Echo I was asked to do Treadmill test wherein I was asked to walk on a treadmill for say 5 minutes.
Before getting onto the treadmill Ms. Sonal and Sister Shivani briefed me how tests would be done and asked me to change the shirt so that the small, flat, sticky white patch can be put on the chest and then electrodes / wire were attached to them. They'll be attached to an electrocardiogram monitor -- called an EKG - that charts your heart's electrical activity during the test.

Within 15 minutes of both the tests being done, I again met Dr. Agrawal with the reports where he declared me fit and fine.  He gave me a fitness certificate which I shall be submitting to my new company !
I was very happy with the service and appreciated the time he gave me and my mother. He explained the entire process of Heart function and was always smiling.

Once again thank you very much Dr. Brijesh Agrwal. I Am very thankful for a quick check up and detailed explanation.

P.s - Incase someone is looking for a good Gynecologist, then I would also suggest to check with Dr. Pradnya Supe who sits in the same clinic.

Regards,
Anuj Saini
